---
title: Create an markdown page
description: >
  How to create an markdown page for your LightNet media site. 
  Using the example of an about page is a common page that provides information about your ministry or community.
---

import { FileTree, Steps } from "@astrojs/starlight/components";

This chapter guides you through creating a markdown page. It uses the example of an about page.
The about page is a common page that provides information about your ministry or community.

<Steps>
    1. **Create Files**: Start by creating a markdown file for each locale.
        For example, if your site supports English and German, you would create the following files:
        <FileTree>
        - src
          - pages
            - en
              - about.md
            - de
              - about.md
        </FileTree>

    1. **Add file content**: Use [Markdown syntax](https://learnxinyminutes.com/markdown/) to write your content. The content of the `/en/about.md` file could look like this:

        ```markdown title="src/pages/en/about.md"
        ---
        layout: "lightnet/layouts/MarkdownPage.astro"
        title: About
        ---

        # About

        Some text about your ministry or community.

        ![Community Picture](../../assets/my-community-picture.jpg)
        ```

        Set the layout to `lightnet/layouts/MarkdownPage.astro`. This makes sure your page includes the header and looks good on all screen sizes.
        You can also create your own layout if you want to customize the look of the page.
        Astro takes care of optimizing your images that are referenced in the markdown file.
        
    1. **Add About to the main menu**: Add the following code to the `astro.config.mjs` file:
        ```js title="astro.config.mjs" ins={5-9}
        export default defineConfig({
          integrations: [
            lightnet({
              mainMenu: [
                {
                  href: "/about",
                  label: {
                    en: "About",
                  },
                },
              ],
            }),
          ],
        });
        ```
    1. **Translate the menu label directly in config**: For each site language, add the translated label to the locale map used in the previous step.
        For example:
        ```js title="astro.config.mjs"
        label: {
          en: "About",
          de: "Über uns",
        }
        ```
    </Steps>
